children: SoftBank Group CEO Masayoshi Son is seeking to raise up to $100 billion from Gulf investors to fund a new wave of artificial intelligence investments, the Financial Times reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.
Son has held discussions in recent weeks with senior figures in the Gulf, including in the United Arab Emirates, regarding a potential fundraising effort, the report said.
The proposed capital raise comes as SoftBank accelerates its AI ambitions, betting heavily on the rapid adoption of generative AI technologies.

Last week, SoftBank said it had completed the final tranche of its $30 billion follow-on investment in OpenAI, taking its cumulative investment in the ChatGPT developer higher as the Japanese technology investor deepens its exposure to the AI sector.

The Gulf has emerged as a key source of capital for global technology and AI projects, with sovereign wealth funds and state-backed investors in the UAE and Saudi Arabia increasingly backing AI, data centre and semiconductor-related ventures.
(Writing by Brinda Darasha; editing by Seban Scaria)

title: SoftBank CEO seeks up to $100bln from Gulf investors for new AI push - report
